mechanism.name: Pointwise conditional mean in the Wang-Yang (2007) d=30 additive heteroscedastic design

generation_equations.label: 1. Scalar stream
generation_equations.expression: Z_s iid N(0,1) conditional on -2.5<=Z_s<=2.5, s=0..n+29-1; rejection sampling; sd=1 before truncation. One scalar truncated-normal stream; source d=30, bound=2.5.

generation_equations.label: 2. Lag window
generation_equations.expression: X_t=(Z_(t+29),Z_(t+28),...,Z_t), t=0..n-1; X1 is the most recent lag. Deterministic window; no new noise. Adjacent rows share 29 stream values.

generation_equations.label: 3. Mean and scale
generation_equations.expression: m(X)=sum_(a=1)^30 sin(pi*X_a/2.5); L=mean(abs(X_a)); sigma(X)=0.1*(sqrt(30)/2)*(5-exp(L))/(5+exp(L)). Deterministic; signed source multiplier retained. Divisor 2 is outside the radical.

generation_equations.label: 4. Innovation
generation_equations.expression: epsilon_t iid N(0,1), independent of the scalar stream and other innovations. Noise sd=1 before multiplication by sigma(X).

generation_equations.label: 5. Outcome and columns
generation_equations.expression: Y_t=m(X_t)+sigma(X_t)*epsilon_t; return X1..X30,Y in chronological window order. Conditional variance=sigma(X_t)^2; no latent/noiseless column is exported.

evidence.expression: Z_s iid N(0,1) conditional on -2.5<=Z_s<=2.5, s=0..n+29-1

sampling.unit: observation row (one simulated time index t together with its 30 covariate coordinates X1..X30)
sampling.dependence: Under the declared lag-window interpretation, rows at distance at least d=30 use disjoint innovations and covariate draws; adjacent rows share 29 coordinates. Consecutive length-30 blocks still overlap in their underlying covariate draws and are not independent. There is no statistic-independent effective sample size.

assumptions: The displayed lag subscripts are interpreted as one shared iid truncated-normal stream, independent of the iid N(0,1) innovations.
The query is fixed inside the 30-dimensional truncated-normal support.
The noise multiplier may have either sign; conditional variance is its square and conditional mean is zero.
Pointwise truth does not imply an estimator or coverage result; the source's unspecified cross-row sampling algorithm remains an interpretation boundary.

properties.notes: All 30 covariates enter the additive sine mean. The source uses n=500,1000,1500,2000, so d=30 is multivariate but not a d>=n sparse high-dimensional design. Nonlinear=true for sine functions. Interactions=false refers to the additive conditional mean; the noise multiplier is a nonseparable nonlinear function of the aggregate L. Observed columns=31.

estimand.name: m(x0) = E[Y | X = x0] = sum_{alpha=1}^{30} sin(pi * x0_alpha / 2.5)
estimand.definition: Scalar conditional mean of Y at a fixed 30-dimensional query point x0 in the superpopulation defined by the fixed Example 6.2 DGP. It is a pointwise regression functional, not a causal effect; the query is a parameter of each scenario and is read from config by truth(config).

truth.expression: Scalar conditional mean of Y at a fixed 30-dimensional query point x0 in the superpopulation defined by the fixed Example 6.2 DGP. It is a pointwise regression functional, not a causal effect; the query is a parameter of each scenario and is read from config by truth(config).
truth.derivation: Closed-form m(x0)=sum sin(pi*x0_alpha/2.5); independently evaluated and checked by quadrature and Monte Carlo. Table-mean signal variance uses exact scalar-stream overlap counts; the noise part uses observed conditional innovation variance. Adjacent length-d blocks are not assumed independent. Numerical estimated_error is a floating-point allowance, not a statistical error.

adaptations: Read the displayed X_{t-alpha} subscripts consistently across rows as overlapping windows of one iid truncated-normal stream. This is the declared interpretation of the source notation; no claim is made that an author implementation has been recovered.
Replace component-estimator comparisons by scalar m(x0)=E[Y|X=x0]; x0=(1.25,0,...,0) and the zero vector are our choices.
Implement truncation by rejection sampling; retain the source's signed noise multiplier without clipping.

For the shared-stream interpretation, use exact overlap counts for signal variance of the whole-table mean and conditional noise variance; adjacent length-d blocks are dependent, and no universal n/d effective sample size is assumed.
Use interface sample sizes and CPU checks without fitting the source estimators.
